title: Beyond the Protocol: Unveiling Attack Vectors in the Model Context Protocol (MCP) Ecosystem
V91_REASON: End-to-end empirical MCP attack study demonstrates malicious servers can trigger harmful local actions (private-file access/device control/digital-asset transfer), but the paper exposes vulnerabilities and finds current audits insufficient rather than implementing a mechanism that preserves/revalidates validity before commit.
V91_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: IEEE TSE DOI 10.1109/TSE.2026.3694876; official abstract/full public preprint

title: Security threat modeling for emerging AI-agent protocols: A comparative analysis of MCP, A2A, agora, and ANP
V91_REASON: Protocol-centric threat model identifies missing mandatory validation/attestation for executable components and quantifies wrong-provider tool execution. This directly motivates execution-boundary validation, but is threat/risk analysis rather than an implemented governed commit mechanism.
V91_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: Journal of Information Security and Applications 104645; arXiv 2602.11327
